newsitem.title: UK: Wall Street's weakness blunts Euro share gains.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street's weakness blunts Euro share gains.

text.p: European shares surrendered some of their gains when Wall Street opened weaker on Thursday after the lastest crop of U.S. economic data reminded traders that inflationary fears are still stalking the markets.
"Rate concerns just won't go away...the housing numbers have put pressure on the bond market," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist for Fahnestock & Co in the United States.
U.S. housing starts jumped 4.5 percent in August to a 1.525 million annual rate against a revised 1.460 million in July, the U.S. Commerce Department said earlier.
Economists polled by Reuters on average had expected starts to slip to 1.445 million against 1.455 million in July.
Economists said the strong figures pointed to an economy unlikely to slow dramatically into the first quarter of 1997.
At one point Wall Street was down around 27 points, though by around 1400 GMT it was down 10.73 at 5866.63.

In London, Europe's premier bourse, leading shares were some 23 points or, 0.6 percent higher, after being up around 30 points, or 0.75 percent, at midday, after heavy derivative-related trading drove prices to a record high of 3,987.7.

"The housing starts came in stronger than we were looking for and that won't help nerves ahead of the FOMC meeting...we see a quarter point rise as likely," a London share trader said, referring to the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market's Committee meeting on September 24, which may increase U.S interest rates.
Among major movers, pharmaceuticals group Zeneca soared as high as 1,630p on renewed takeover speculation. The stock slipped back to trade 44-1/2p higher at 1,589p at 1415 GMT.
French financial markets digested a small cut by the Bank of France to a key interest rate on in an apparent sign of its approval of the conservative government's 1997 budget.
The Bank said it was lowering its intervention rate to 3.25 percent from 3.35 percent at a money market tender.
The Bank left the five-to-10 day rate, which is considered less important at the moment, unchanged at 4.75 percent.
"It means the Bank of France did not see the budget as being a threat in terms of inflation or the franc," a French bank economist said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index of French shares was up 13.11 points or 0.63 percent at 2,085.84 at 1130 GMT. The index had been up 0.57 percent just before the rate reduction, but by mid-afternoon it was just 7.8 points higher at 2080.53. The franc was trading at 3.4063 per mark shortly after the rate cut, lower than before the budget announcement but off the low of 3.4092 it reached on Wednesday when the government unveiled its 1997 budget. At 1400 gmt it was at 3.4054 per mark.
The budget lowered spending in real terms to allow France to meet Maastricht treaty criteria on European monetary union.

German shares opened mostly flat and showed no inclination to move in either direction after data showing German August money supply growth came in above forecasts and a new business climate index showed confidence improving slightly.
In the foreign exchanges, the dollar continued an easier bias, though it edged higher against the mark, dealers said. It was steady against the yen.

Many in the market are quite bullish for a near-term dollar upturn but its failure to break higher at the end of last week disappointed and the market has been quick to take profits. "With the next Fed move certain to be up, whether it's next week or not, the dollar does have more to do on the upside," said one trader at a leading U.S. bank in London.
"But people have been stung a few times in the past when the dollar failed to perform and no one wants to take the plunge."
Traders were a little surprised that stronger than expected money supply figures from Germany had very little impact.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5125 marks and 109.12 yen compared with 1.5091 marks and 109.12 yen in Europe late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 23.3 points at 3,970.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 7.8 points at 2,080.53.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 1.26 at 2,624.44.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1400
Gold was fixed at $382.75 after closing in London at $383.35 on Wednesday.
